easy.def: A loud sound that warns you.
examples: The fire alarm rang.
An alarm woke me.
The alarm is loud.

more.def: A loud sound or signal that warns of danger or wakes you up.
examples: The fire alarm rang in the school.
My alarm woke me at seven.
The car alarm went off.

easy.def: A word used to show sadness.
examples: Alas, the party is over.
Alas, I cannot go.
Alas, it is gone.

more.def: A word used in a story or poem to show that you feel sad or sorry.
examples: Alas, the party is over!
Alas, I cannot come to your game this weekend.
Alas, the last cookie was gone.

easy.def: A book for keeping photos or stamps.
examples: I look at the photo album.
My stamp album is full.
The album has old pictures.

more.def: A book with pages for keeping photos, stamps or other things you collect.
examples: We looked through the family photo album.
She put the new stamp in her album.
The album was full of baby pictures.

easy.def: A group of songs sold together.
examples: The singer made an album.
I love this album.
The album has twelve songs.

more.def: A collection of songs that is sold together.
examples: The band released a new album this summer.
My favorite song is on the album.
The album has ten songs.

easy.def: Awake and ready to notice things.
examples: The dog is alert.
Stay alert on the trail.
The guard was alert.

more.def: Watching and ready to notice or react to what is going on.
examples: The alert deer lifted its head at the slightest sound.
Stay alert when you cross the street.
After a good night's sleep, she felt fresh and alert.
The bell alerted the class.
I alert Mom.
The alarm alerts us.

more.def: To warn someone about a danger or something important.
examples: The siren alerted people about the storm.
My barking dog alerted us to the stranger.
She alerted the teacher to the broken window.
The spy used an alias.
He had an alias.
The alias was Bob.

more.def: A different name that a person uses instead of their real name.
examples: The writer published under an alias.
The author wrote under an alias.
His alias was Captain Hook.

easy.def: A creature from another planet in stories.
examples: The alien had green skin.
The movie is about an alien.
I drew an alien.

more.def: A pretend visitor from another planet in stories and movies.
examples: The alien stepped out of the spaceship.
In the movie, an alien made friends with a boy.
I drew an alien with three eyes.
It felt alien to be in a new place.
The alien land was strange.
The food seemed alien.

more.def: Strange, unfamiliar or from another place.
examples: The new city felt alien to her at first.
An alien smell filled the air.
The customs seemed alien to the visitors.
The twins look alike.
The two cats are alike.
We think alike.

more.def: Very similar, not different.
examples: The twins look so alike that few can tell them apart.
The two puppies are alike in color.
My friend and I think alike.
The fish is alive.
Plants are alive.
Is the bug still alive?

more.def: Living, and not dead.
examples: The scientists found a tiny animal that was still alive.
Plants are alive even though they do not move around.
The old tree is still alive and grows new leaves each spring.
All the kids can play.
I ate all my peas.
She read all the books.

more.def: The whole amount of something, or every one of a group.
examples: All the students lined up for the fire drill.
We stayed inside all day because of the rain.
The squirrel hid all of the acorns before winter.

easy.def: Being loyal to a country, a leader or a cause.
examples: I pledge allegiance.
I have allegiance to my team.
She showed her allegiance.

more.def: Loyalty to a country, a person, a group or a cause.
examples: We pledge allegiance to the flag.
I have allegiance to my team and always cheer for it.
She showed her allegiance by helping the club.

easy.def: Getting a rash or sneezing because of something like cats.
examples: I am allergic to cats.
She is allergic to nuts.
He is allergic to dust.

more.def: Having a bad reaction, such as sneezing or a rash, to something that is harmless to most people.
examples: I am allergic to cats and sneeze around them.
She is allergic to peanuts.
He is allergic to pollen in spring.

easy.def: When your body reacts badly to something that is not harmful to most people.
examples: I have an allergy to peanuts.
My sister has an allergy to cats.
An allergy can make you sneeze.

more.def: A reaction of the body, such as sneezing or itching, to something like pollen, dust or certain foods.
examples: I have an allergy to cats, so I sneeze when I pet them.
Spring flowers can cause an allergy and a runny nose.
A food allergy means you must stay away from the food that makes you sick.
The cat walked down the alley.
The alley is narrow.
We cut through the alley.

more.def: A narrow street or path between buildings.
examples: The cat slipped down the alley.
We took a shortcut through the alley behind the shop.
Trash cans lined the alley.

easy.def: A group that joins together to help each other.
examples: The two countries made an alliance.
They formed an alliance.
The alliance was strong.

more.def: A joining together of people, groups or countries to help each other and work toward the same goal.
examples: The two countries formed an alliance and promised to help each other.
The three clubs made an alliance to hold one big fair.
An alliance between the farmers and the town gave everyone fresh food.

easy.def: Joined together to help each other.
examples: The allied countries helped each other.
They were allied teams.
We are allied in this game.

more.def: Joined together with others to work toward the same goal, often as countries do in a war or for trade.
examples: The allied countries agreed to share food and supplies.
The two allied teams worked together to solve the puzzle.
Allied nations signed a promise to help each other.

easy.def: A big animal with a long mouth and sharp teeth that lives in swamps.
examples: The alligator swam in the pond.
An alligator has sharp teeth.
We saw an alligator at the zoo.

more.def: A large reptile with a broad snout, thick skin and a strong tail that lives in warm swamps and rivers.
examples: An alligator lay still in the sun along the riverbank.
Alligators lay their eggs in nests made of plants and mud.
The guide steered the boat quietly past an alligator in the swamp.
Mom will allow me to stay up late.
The pool does not allow running.
Dad allowed us to have one more cookie.

more.def: To give permission for someone to do or have something.
examples: The museum does not allow visitors to touch the paintings.
Our teacher allows us to read quietly after a test.
Dogs are not allowed inside the bakery.
I get an allowance.
My allowance is five dollars.
I saved my allowance.

more.def: Money that a child gets regularly from a parent.
examples: I get an allowance every Saturday.
I spent my allowance on a book.
She saved her allowance for a bike.

easy.def: A friend or partner who helps you.
examples: The two countries are allies.
He was my ally in the game.
Allies help each other.

more.def: A person or country that joins with another to help.
examples: The two countries were allies in the war.
My brother was my ally when I needed help.
Bees are allies of the garden.
The almighty king ruled.
The Almighty is another name for God.
An almighty roar came.

more.def: Having complete power, or very great.
examples: The king in the story seemed almighty.
The word almighty is sometimes used for God.
An almighty crash shook the room.
I am almost done.
It is almost bedtime.
We almost missed the bus.

more.def: Very nearly, but not completely.
examples: The glass was almost full, so I poured slowly.
It was almost midnight when the train arrived.
She almost won the race, but another runner passed her at the end.

easy.def: A Hawaiian word used to say hello or goodbye.
examples: Aloha, friends!
We said aloha at the beach.
The hula dancer said aloha.

more.def: A word from Hawaii that people use to say hello or goodbye, and that also stands for love and kindness.
examples: The guide greeted us with a cheerful "Aloha!" when we arrived in Hawaii.
She waved and said aloha as the boat left the harbor.
In Hawaii, aloha is both a friendly greeting and a way of showing kindness.
I was alone.
She likes to be alone.
He played alone.

more.def: By yourself, with nobody else.
examples: The lighthouse keeper lived alone on the rocky island.
She likes to read alone in the quiet room.
He did not feel alone with his dog beside him.
I walked alone.
She did it alone.
Can you carry it alone?

more.def: Without any help or company from others.
examples: I made the whole model airplane alone.
He walked home alone after school.
Wolves often hunt together, but a bear usually hunts alone.

easy.def: Next to or following a path.
examples: We walked along the river.
Trees grow along the road.
A line of ducks swam along the shore.

more.def: Following the length of something, such as a road, river or wall.
examples: Bicycle riders pedaled along the path beside the lake.
Pretty flowers grew along the garden wall.
The train rolled slowly along the tracks.
Come along!
Bring your dog along.
Can I come along?

more.def: Together with someone else.
examples: We are going to the zoo, and you can come along.
She brought her little sister along to the swimming pool.
Can you bring a snack along for the trip?
The boat sailed alongside the ship.
I walked alongside Dad.
The path runs alongside the river.

more.def: At the side of, or together with.
examples: The small boat sailed alongside the ship.
I walked alongside Dad to the store.
A young dolphin swam alongside its mother.

easy.def: All the letters we use to write, from A to Z.
examples: I know the alphabet.
We sang the alphabet song.
The alphabet has 26 letters.

more.def: The set of letters, in order, that are used to write the words of a language.
examples: The English alphabet has twenty-six letters, from A to Z.
We sang the alphabet song to learn the order of the letters.
Words in a dictionary are listed in the order of the alphabet.
I already ate.
The movie already started.
She is already here.

more.def: Before this time, or sooner than you thought.
examples: I already finished my homework.
The bus has already left.
It is already time for lunch.
I also like cake.
She also sings.
He is also here.

more.def: In addition, or as well as something already said.
examples: Frogs live in water, and they also live on land.
She plays the violin and also sings in the choir.
The park has swings, and there is also a pond.

easy.def: A table in a place of worship.
examples: The altar was in the church.
Flowers sat on the altar.
The altar is stone.

more.def: A table or raised place in a church or temple where religious acts are done.
examples: The candles stood on the altar.
Flowers were placed on the altar.
The altar was made of stone.
I alter my plan.
The tailor altered the dress.
Rain altered our plans.

more.def: To make something a little different.
examples: The tailor altered the dress to fit me.
Rain altered our plans for the picnic.
He altered the recipe by adding more spice.
We go on alternate days.
The alternate road is longer.
We have an alternate plan.

more.def: Happening or coming every second time; or another choice.
examples: We meet on alternate Fridays.
We took an alternate road because of the traffic.
I made an alternate plan in case it rained.

easy.def: To take turns, one after the other.
examples: We alternate days.
The lights alternate red and green.
They alternate turns.

more.def: To change back and forth between two things, one after the other.
examples: We alternate who sets the table each night.
The lights alternated between red and green.
The weather alternated between sun and rain all week.
We need an alternative.
Walking is an alternative.
Pizza is an alternative to pasta.

more.def: A different choice that you can make instead of the first one.
examples: Walking is an alternative if the bus is late.
We found an alternative to the broken swing.
Fruit is a healthy alternative to candy.
Although it rained, we played.
He ran, although he was tired.
I like pie, although I am full.

more.def: In spite of the fact that; even though.
examples: Although it was cold, we went outside.
She smiled, although she was nervous.
We stayed, although the movie was long.

easy.def: How high something is above the ground or the sea.
examples: The plane flew at a high altitude.
A mountain has a high altitude.
The altitude was big.

more.def: The height of something above the level of the sea or the ground.
examples: The plane flew at a high altitude above the clouds.
It is hard to breathe at the high altitude of the mountain.
The balloon rose to an altitude of one thousand feet.
Altogether, we had ten.
There are five altogether.
The cost was ten dollars altogether.

more.def: All together, or in total.
examples: Altogether, we had ten dollars.
There are five of us altogether.
The trip was altogether too long.

easy.def: All the time, or every time.
examples: I always brush my teeth.
The sun always rises.
She is always happy.

more.def: At all times, or every time, without change.
examples: The sun always rises in the east.
My grandmother always sings when she cooks.
He is always the first one to arrive at school.
